finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so the authorization check is never enforced. Any caller can delete any account. closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which shows the intended behavior.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sending DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id they do not own and without admin rights.
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at AccountService.java:23, which deletes the account.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the entry point for DELETE /accounts/{id}; id is attacker-controlled
Account is looked up by the attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is ignored, so no exception is thrown when the user is unauthorized

finding.guards_checked: canDelete at line 10 would enforce admin or owner, but its result is unused on this path. There is no assertCanDelete call, no other authorization layer, and no exception. The only file in the directory is this one, so no controller or filter-level checks were visible. Compare closeAccount at line 29, which uses assertCanDelete and is correct.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (line 9) returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at line 22, so nothing enforces it. assertCanDelete (line 13) throws but is only used in closeAccount (line 29). No other guard exists in the only file present.
verdict.reason: AccountService.java:22 discards the boolean returned by canDelete, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated non-owner, non-admin caller, unlike closeAccount at line 29 which uses the throwing assertCanDelete.

verdict_facts.guard_found: canDelete (line 9-11) returns a boolean, but its result is discarded at line 22; no assertCanDelete, exception, or other check on this path.
verdict_facts.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the boolean from canDelete() is a bare statement and is ignored, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user, unlike closeAccount which uses the throwing assertCanDelete at line 29.
